node: Travel capacity enablers: airport services, baggage handling, maintenance, lodging operations software, and local experience infrastructure
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found direct US-listed exposure concentrated in aviation aftermarket/MRO, engine leasing and maintenance, hospitality operating software, and destination experience assets. The best underfollowed lane candidates are not airlines or hotels themselves, but companies whose revenue can be pulled by aircraft utilization, hotel/resort complexity, and constrained destination capacity. No clean US-listed pure-play baggage-handling or airport ground-handling contractor was identified in this focused pass; that remains a coverage gap for later searches. Expanded the underfollowed universe around travel-capacity enablers rather than airlines, hotels, cruise lines, or OTAs. The strongest US-listed candidates in this pass cluster around aircraft maintenance/parts, airport labor/services, hospitality operating software, and airport ground-support/baggage/gate equipment. These are capacity-adjacent names that may benefit when travel demand stresses maintenance turnaround, airport staffing, gate/baggage infrastructure, and hotel operating complexity. No recommendation is implied; this is a Layer 1B research universe only. Expanded the underfollowed discovery lane for travel-capacity enablers. The strongest US-listed candidates found in this pass sit one or two layers away from obvious travel demand: aviation aftermarket parts and MRO capacity, hospitality operating software, and airport concession/regulated infrastructure. The lane is intentionally not airlines, hotels, cruise lines, or online travel agencies; those remain demand indicators and customer/context anchors.
